statement: Every quasi-etale cover of a Gorenstein non-klt lc surface germ is tame at every exceptional divisorial valuation

statement: Proper surface punctures have finitely generated pi1 when every omitted singularity has one smooth elliptic exceptional curve
depends_on: D:single-curve-residue-tameness; Stacks0C5P; projective tame quotient; finite normalization descent

statement: Finite global images of all punctured strict-local groups suffice for arbitrary codimension-two boundaries without a uniform bound
depends_on: CSK2023 Theorem3.7 pp708-709; Stibitz2017 Theorem2 and section4; finite local intersection stabilization; Galois tower contradiction
notes: Extends D:finite-local-images from finite Y to arbitrary Y. It suffices to test geometric closed points. Source local groups may be infinite. No quasi-projectivity assumption.

statement: Proper normal threefolds in characteristic p>5 have finitely generated punctured pi1 whenever they are klt near an arbitrary codimension-two boundary
depends_on: CSK2023 Setup1.1 and TheoremA pp694-695, Cor4.5 p714; D:finite-local-images-arbitrary

statement: Finite global images of punctured strict-local groups suffice for a finite boundary
depends_on: Finite-image avoidance; normalization and strict-local extension; SGA1 X2.9; BCGST2019 Cor4.2 second proof

depends_on: Stein factorization; p-rank-one separability; geometric reducedness; D:vertical-fibration-multiplicity
notes: Includes quasi-elliptic generic fibres. No projectivity, lc, Q-factoriality or formally graded local hypothesis; arbitrary finite omitted singularities are allowed.

statement: The vertical-fibration finite-generation criteria descend under proper birational maps and finite normalization
depends_on: Generic-field connected pullback; SGA1 IX5.2 finite proper descent

depends_on: Hoshi2006 Proposition2.1/Theorem2.3 pp13-16 andA.10 pp57-58; fixed component multiplicities bound base wild inertia; tame curve group

statement: Every original fixed boundary on a normal proper surface mapping nonconstantly to a proper curve has finitely generated tame quotient

notes: Arbitrary horizontal and vertical boundary; original generic curve need not be smooth and original horizontal points need not be separable. Only a genuine morphism to a proper curve is used; a rational pencil on a resolution does not settle the general gate.

depends_on: Stacks0BTX arithmetic exactness; normal generic connectedness; Stacks056V dense smooth locus; full or wild base inertia multiplicity bounds

statement: Every vertical boundary on a normal proper scheme mapping to a curve has finitely generated fixed-boundary quotient; full pi1 is finitely generated if every fibre is met
depends_on: D:generic-fibre-generation proof; proper geometric generic fibre finite generation; Stein factorization and p-rank-one regularity

statement: Projective normalization of the geometric generic fibre gives finite generation for every fixed boundary in arbitrary dimension
depends_on: Finite purely inseparable geometric normalization; D:fixed-boundary-positive; D:generic-fibre-generation; finite radicial tame pullback

depends_on: Stacks0BXT geometric normalization; separable extensions cannot absorb pure algebraic extensions
notes: The bound divides [F0:F] and depends only on M/F, not the varying finite L/F. This controls fierce residue contributions in the projective-base theorem.

statement: A finitely generated geometric generic group gives fixed-boundary finite generation over any normal projective base
depends_on: Stacks0BTX/056V; normalization under smooth base change03GV; fpqc etale descent02VN; uniform e_p*f_insep bound09EE/0BUA; projective fixed-boundary group
notes: All dimensions. A single retained smooth-surjective base open makes every constant-field quotient genuinely etale, including codimension2. Geometric generic fibre is integral; full or normal fixed-boundary generic group may be used.

statement: Vertical boundary and projective reduced-geometric-generic normalization imply fixed-boundary finite generation over arbitrary projective images
depends_on: D:projective-base-generation; Stein constant field; finite pure normalization; topological invariance and original tame DVR pullback
notes: Includes every generic fibre of dimension at most one. The original geometric generic fibre may be nonreduced. For codimension-at-least-two boundary the conclusion is full pi1.

statement: Projective-base generation needs only D1 for all boundaries on every finite normal cover of the base

notes: Base is projective. All finite normal connected covers at every stage are included, even inseparable ones. Generic fibre dimension<=1 suffices; every arrow is an original proper-scheme morphism.

depends_on: AHLS2026 Proposition3.1.8, Definition3.2.4, Theorem3.5.1; proper valuative criterion
notes: Every test valuation acquires a centre by properness; its strictly henselian local Kummer group is pro-prime-to-residue-characteristic. Thus full ket equals relative tame ket.

statement: Proper log regular pairs have finitely generated original fixed-boundary tame quotient without projectivity or underlying regularity
notes: The cover comparison tests exactly original codimension-one boundary points. No claim that an arbitrary singular compactification is log regular; recognition theorem only.

This is a geometric ramification counterexample, not a counterexample to D1/D2 finite generation.26 exact polynomial assertions passed.

statement: Exact first and higher curve obstruction conditions produce an actual finite cone cover after completion

notes: Applies to nonabelian covers of arbitrary degree and to strict henselization. The same finite-index wild subgroup is killed by every pulled-back cover; original and completed boundary DVRs are compared exactly.

statement: A sole smooth exceptional curve of degree d>max(0,2g-2) has finite full wild inertia image

notes: Choose q=p^r with q(d-2g+2)>2g-2 and qd>2g-2; the full wild image has order at most q. Finiteness, not tameness, is asserted.

depends_on: Kummer03PK; semilinear Fitting and Frobenius-fixed basis; Artin-Schreier0A3J; genus formula

statement: At d=2g-2, torsion omega_C tensor N gives finite full wild image, including every Q-Gorenstein index

notes: With the same integer c>=1 in both bounds, at most c+2 generators suffice. Finite crown inputs use CFSG. Neither uniform geometric bound is asserted for the residual D cases.
